monthly_review.summary: You increased volume and intensity this month, with faster paces and higher HR across more kilometers — a clear step toward improved aerobic capacity and race readiness.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved (+0.13 m/km per bpm) despite higher average HR and faster pace — indicating better cardiovascular economy at higher intensities.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance by 8.5 km and matched the number of runs — no additional running is needed to surpass May’s totals.

insights.title: Efficiency gains under load
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.55 m/km per bpm while avg pace improved and avg HR increased — suggesting improved stroke volume or oxygen extraction at sub-threshold efforts.

insights.title: Shift toward threshold work
insights.body: Zone 3 distribution increased from 19% to 28%, and Zone 4 rose from 3% to 14%, while Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 56% — signaling intentional progression into lactate threshold territory.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff at endurance pace
insights.body: Cadence increased +5 spm (146 → 151), yet stride length decreased in long runs (e.g., 69.52 cm on 11.0 km @ 9:14/km vs 91.13 cm on 3.0 km @ 6:32/km), indicating form preservation at fatigue — likely aided by reduced vertical oscillation (7.7–7.2 cm) during longer efforts.

insights.title: Low-intensity recovery run underutilized
insights.body: Only 1% of June time was spent in Zone 5, but your slowest recent run (10:50/km, HR 112 bpm, 145 spm) was fully in Zone 1 — yet it delivered only 1.6 TE, suggesting opportunity to extend duration or frequency of true recovery sessions to support higher-intensity adaptation.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-min Zone 1 run (HR ≤125 bpm) before June ends — aim for cadence ≥145 spm and ground contact <330 ms.
recommendations.reason: Your most recent Zone 1 run (10:50/km, HR 112) had elevated ground contact (344 ms) and low TE (1.6); extending duration at low HR will reinforce recovery physiology without compromising form.

recommendations.action: Add 1x 6-min Zone 4 interval (HR 160–168 bpm) embedded in your next 10-km run — e.g., after 3 km, do 6 min at Zone 4, then resume Zone 3 for remainder.
recommendations.reason: Zone 4 volume jumped to 14% this month but remains underdeveloped relative to your rising VO2 max (37→39) and aerobic TE consistency; targeted Zone 4 boosts lactate clearance capacity.

recommendations.action: After your next long run (>9 km), perform 3×1-min strides (90 sec walk recovery) focusing on cadence ≥165 spm and vertical oscillation <7.0 cm.
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent run (392 sec/km = 6:32/km) showed 162 spm and 8.4 cm vertical oscillation — lowering VO reduces energy waste and supports efficiency gains observed this month.

weekly_focus.description: Blend sustained Zone 3/4 efforts to solidify lactate threshold gains while deliberately restoring autonomic balance through structured low-HR running and neuromuscular priming.
